485. ///
486. /// # Description
487. ///
488. /// Ensures that a page table exists for the given PDE index in the kernel page directory. If the
489. /// PDE is already present, returns the physical address of the existing page table. Otherwise,
490. /// allocates a new page table from the BSS pool, installs the PDE, and returns the new page
491. /// table's physical address.
492. ///
493. /// # Parameters
494. ///
495. /// - `pd`: The kernel page directory table.
496. /// - `pde_idx`: The page directory index to check.
497. ///
498. /// # Returns
499. ///
500. /// Upon success, the physical address of the page table is returned. Upon failure, an error is
501. /// returned instead.
502. ///
503. /// # Errors
504. ///
505. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read the PDE.
506. /// - [`ErrorCode::OutOfMemory`]: No BSS page table slots available.
507. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: The allocated page table frame number is out of range.
508. ///
509. #[verus_spec(result =>
510.     requires
511.         identity_map_view().inv(),
512.     ensures
513.         identity_map_view().inv(),
514.         match result {
515.             // The returned page-table physical address is page-aligned (BSS-backed and
516.             // immediately usable as `Table::from_address` for the follow-up `ensure_pte`).
517.             // Ensuring a page table installs internal structure only -- it adds no page to the
518.             // identity map.
519.             Ok(pt_paddr) => spec_is_page_aligned(pt_paddr as int),
520.             Err(_) => true,
521.         },
522. )]
523. fn ensure_pt(pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry>, pde_idx: TableIndex) -> Result<usize, Error> {
524.     proof! { admit(); }
525.     let pde: PageDirectoryEntry = unsafe { pd.read(pde_idx) }.ok_or_else(|| {
526.         let reason: &str = "invalid PDE read from kernel PD";
527.         #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
528.         error!("ensure_pt(): {reason}");
529.         Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
530.     })?;
531. 
532.     if pde.is_present() {
533.         return Ok(pde.frame_address());
534.     }
535. 
536.     // No PT exists — allocate one from the BSS pool (zeroed = all PTEs absent).
537.     // SAFETY: atomic bump allocator ensures exclusive access to the slot;
538.     // BSS is zero-initialized, so assume_init_mut() is sound for integer arrays.
539.     let slot: &'static mut [PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH] = unsafe {
540.         PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR
541.             .alloc_as::<[PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH]>()
542.             .map_err(|e| {
543.                 #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
544.                 error!("ensure_pt(): page table allocation failed: {}", e);
545.                 Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, "BSS page table allocation failed")
546.             })?
547.             .assume_init_mut()
548.     };
549.     let pt_paddr: usize = slot.as_ptr() as usize;
550. 
551.     // Install the PDE with type-safe flag constructors.
552.     let pt_frame: FrameNumber =
553.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(pt_paddr / mem::PAGE_SIZE).ok_or_else(|| {
554.             let reason: &str = "BSS page table frame number out of range";
555.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
556.             error!("ensure_pt(): {reason}");
557.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason)
558.         })?;
559.     let new_pde: PageDirectoryEntry = PageDirectoryEntry::new(
560.         PageDirectoryEntryFlags::new(
561.             PresentFlag::Present,
562.             ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite,
563.             UserSupervisorFlag::Supervisor,
564.             PageWriteThroughFlag::NotWriteThrough,
565.             PageCacheDisableFlag::CacheEnabled,
566.             AccessedFlag::NotAccessed,
567.             DirtyFlag::NotDirty,
568.             PageSizeFlag::Standard,
569.         ),
570.         pt_frame,
571.     );
572.     // SAFETY: the kernel PD is identity-mapped.
573.     unsafe { pd.write(pde_idx, new_pde) };
574. 
575.     Ok(pt_paddr)
576. }
577. 
578. ///
579. /// # Description
580. ///
581. /// Ensures that a page table entry for the given index is identity-mapped. If the PTE is already
582. /// present, this function is a no-op. Otherwise, it creates a new identity-mapped PTE and
583. /// invalidates the corresponding TLB entry.
584. ///
585. /// # Parameters
586. ///
587. /// - `pt`: The page table to write into.
588. /// - `pte_idx`: The page table index to check.
589. /// - `phys_addr`: The physical address to identity-map (used as both frame source and TLB target).
590. ///
591. /// # Returns
592. ///
593. /// Upon success, empty is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
594. ///
595. /// # Errors
596. ///
597. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read the PTE.
598. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: The frame number is out of range.
599. ///
600. #[verus_spec(result =>
601.     requires
602.         identity_map_view().inv(),
603.     ensures
604.         identity_map_view().inv(),
605.         match result {
606.             // The leaf step that realizes V==P: on success the page containing `phys_addr` is
607.             // present (writable, supervisor) and reachable at its own physical address. Membership
608.             // holds whether the PTE was freshly installed or already present (idempotent).
609.             Ok(_) => identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr as int)),
610.             Err(_) => true,
611.         },
612. )]
613. fn ensure_pte(
614.     pt: Table<PageTableEntry>,
615.     pte_idx: TableIndex,
616.     phys_addr: usize,
617. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
618.     proof! { admit(); }
619.     let pte: PageTableEntry = unsafe { pt.read(pte_idx) }.ok_or_else(|| {
620.         let reason: &str = "invalid PTE read from page table";
621.         #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
622.         error!("ensure_pte(): {reason}");
623.         Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
624.     })?;
625. 
626.     if pte.is_present() {
627.         return Ok(());
628.     }
629. 
630.     // Fill the PTE with an identity mapping.
631.     let frame: FrameNumber =
632.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(phys_addr / mem::PAGE_SIZE).ok_or_else(|| {
633.             let reason: &str = "frame number out of range";
634.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
635.             error!("ensure_pte(): {reason}");
636.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason)
637.         })?;
638.     let new_pte: PageTableEntry = PageTableEntry::new(
639.         PageTableEntryFlags::new(
640.             PresentFlag::Present,
641.             ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite,
642.             UserSupervisorFlag::Supervisor,
643.             PageWriteThroughFlag::NotWriteThrough,
644.             PageCacheDisableFlag::CacheEnabled,
645.             AccessedFlag::NotAccessed,
646.             DirtyFlag::NotDirty,
647.         ),
648.         frame,
649.     );
650.     // SAFETY: the PT is identity-mapped.
651.     unsafe { pt.write(pte_idx, new_pte) };
652. 
653.     // Invalidate the TLB entry for this page.
654.     unsafe { paging::invlpg(phys_addr) };
655. 
656.     Ok(())
657. }
658. 
659. ///
660. /// # Description
661. ///
662. /// Identity-maps a single page in the kernel page directory.
663. ///
664. /// If the target PTE is already present, this function is a no-op. If the PDE is absent, a new
665. /// page table is allocated from the BSS pool and installed before the identity-mapped PTE is
666. /// created.
667. ///
668. /// # Parameters
669. ///
670. /// - `phys_addr`: Page-aligned physical address to identity-map.
671. ///
672. /// # Returns
673. ///
674. /// Upon success, empty is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
675. ///
676. /// # Errors
677. ///
678. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read a valid paging entry.
679. ///
680. /// # Notes
681. ///
682. /// If the lazy mapper has not been initialized yet (boot page tables still active), this function
683. /// is a no-op and returns success.
684. #[verus_spec(result =>
685.     requires
686.         identity_map_view().inv(),
687.     ensures
688.         identity_map_view().inv(),
689.         match result {
690.             // The page containing `phys_addr` is reachable at its own physical address. After init
691.             // this means it is present (writable, supervisor) in the kernel page directory; before
692.             // init the call is a no-op and the boot page tables already cover it. Either way the
693.             // caller (`KernelFrame::new`) may subsequently read/write the frame through `phys_addr`.
694.             Ok(_) => identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
695.             Err(_) => true,
696.         },
697. )]
698. pub(crate) fn identity_map_page(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
699.     proof! { admit(); }
700.     let phys_addr: usize = phys_addr.into_raw_value();
701. 
702.     let pd_paddr: usize = KERNEL_PD_PADDR.load(Ordering::Acquire);
703.     // Check if the lazy mapper has been initialized.
704.     if pd_paddr == 0 {
705.         return Ok(());
706.     }
707. 
708.     let pde_idx: TableIndex = paging::pd_index(phys_addr);
709.     let pte_idx: TableIndex = paging::pt_index(phys_addr);
710. 
711.     // SAFETY: the PD is identity-mapped.
712.     let pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pd_paddr) };
713.     let pt_paddr: usize = ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)?;
714. 
715.     // SAFETY: the PT is identity-mapped (BSS-backed).
716.     let pt: Table<PageTableEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pt_paddr) };
717.     ensure_pte(pt, pte_idx, phys_addr)
718. }

the error paths lack meaningful ensures, which is the same root cause.
There
are also 8 admits in the module (3 in exec, 5 in proof) that need reporting
, especially the exec-body admits that indicate the specs aren't proven. On the transition properties, the view_design lists
monotonicity (`old@.mapped.subset_of(self@.mapped)`) as an ensure, but the current specs omit any old/new relation.
The global uninterpreted model can't express old/new without a threaded token, so `
Err(_) => true` might be defended as a model limitation rather than a fixable issue—but that
defense is weak since the Err arm should at least express state
unchanged, which also requires old/new relations.

`. Since the checklist flags `Err(_) => true` as the canonical anti-pattern and the spec phase produced exactly that three
times, this is a genuine failure that needs fixing by threading a ghost or tracked state token—enabling proper ensures
that capture both the Ok case (accessible
) and the Err case (state unchanged).

klist walk-through and a focused fix request on this top FAIL. The task framing implies a separate fixer responds on subsequent turns, but since I'm running
